title: Google Voice vs Grasshopper: The $7 Workspace Catch
summary: Google Voice costs $10 per user plus a $7 Workspace seat. Grasshopper starts at $14 for one user. See what each costs at 1, 2, 5 and 10 seats.
body_markdown:
Google Voice for business starts at $10 per user per month and Grasshopper at $14, which looks like a $4 gap. But that’s not a like-for-like comparison.


A single US-based individual can use Google Voice’s voice-only plan without Google Workspace. A team also needs Google Workspace, starting at $7 more per person. Grasshopper’s $14 True Solo plan covers one user, one number, and one extension. Adding a second person means moving up to Solo Plus at $25 per month, which includes unlimited users and one number and three extensions.


For one person, Google Voice is cheaper. From the second user on, Grasshopper’s flat plan pricing wins, as long as one number and three extensions are enough.


##


**When to choose Google Voice vs Grasshopper**


Choose Google Voice if:


- Your team already pays for Google Workspace and want to prioritize only Google app integrations.
- You’re a one-person business that wants a simple, inexpensive business number.
-
- You want local numbers beyond just the US or Canada. Google Voice’s team plans are available in 14+ countries and regions.


Choose Grasshopper if:


- You have a team of two or more people. Flat-rate per-account pricing can make Grasshopper cheaper.
- You need a toll-free or vanity number. Google Voice doesn’t offer them and won’t let you port one in either.
- You need to receive faxes on your business number. It’s inbound only, and fax isn’t on any Google Voice plan.
- You want automatic call recording at a lower price.


Just know that neither solution connects to a CRM natively. If you want to log customer conversations into your CRM, like[Salesforce](https://www.quo.com/integrations/salesforce) ,[HubSpot,](https://www.quo.com/integrations/hubspot) or[Pipedrive](https://www.quo.com/integrations/pipedrive) , you have to do it manually. This can leave gaps in your records, especially if your team skips logging when they’re busy.


##


**Google Voice vs Grasshopper cost by team size**


**Google Voice entry price.** Starter is $10 per user per month. A single user can buy a Voice-only version at that price with no Google Workspace subscription. But the Voice-only plan is capped at one user, restricted to the US, and has no ring groups or automatic call recording.


A second user, or being outside the US, moves you to the team version of Starter.


This requires Google Workspace, starting at $7 per user per month. So your real entry cost starts at $17 per user per month. Ring groups require Standard, which brings the cost to $27 per user per month.


**Grasshopper entry price.** True Solo is $14 per month billed annually, or $18 per billed monthly. That figure covers one user, one number, and one extension. If you have more users or want more extensions, you have to upgrade to Solo Plus at $25 per month billed annually, or $32 per month billed monthly.


For a single user, Google Voice is $4 below Grasshopper’s annual rate and $8 below its monthly rate. That changes when you add a second user. Google Voice’s real cost starts at $17 per person, since each user also needs a Workspace seat. On Grasshopper, a second user means moving up to Solo Plus at $25 per month, which covers unlimited users.


The table below compares costs for one, two, five, and 10 users.


Team size Google Voice Grasshopper Note


1 Starter, Voice-only, $10 per month True Solo, $14 per month Google Voice is $4 cheaper, but Voice-only is US-only and lacks features like ring groups. If you’re outside the US, you have to add a Workspace subscription, which brings your bill to at least $17 per user per month. An auto-attendant adds $10 on the voice-only plan, and ring groups require the team plan at about $27 per user.


2 Starter, $34 per month Solo Plus, $25 per month Grasshopper is cheaper from the second seat and stays less expensive than Google Voice at every team-size above it.


5 Starter, $85 per month Solo Plus, $25 per month Google Voice costs 3.4x more. Grasshopper’s constraint is extensions, not seats — five people share three routing destinations.


10 Starter, $170 per month Solo Plus, $25 per month Google Voice Starter maxes at 10 users. Beyond that, you have to upgrade to Voice Standard, at $27 per user per month including Workspace, or Premier, at $37 per user per month. If you want more numbers or extensions with Grasshopper, you can upgrade to Small Business, at $55 per month.


Google Voice also doesn’t offer annual billing. So the monthly price is the cheapest it will get. Grasshopper discounts roughly 22% for annual billing, or $14 versus $18 on True Solo and $55 versus $70 on Small Business.


##


**Google Voice vs Grasshopper plans at a glance**


Let’s compare the two business phone systems’ base plans: Google Voice Starter, Voice-only, and Grasshopper True Solo.
